'''Michael Joseph Kelly''' (born 14 May 1949) is a [[New Zealand]]-[[UK|British]] [[physicist]].  He was Prince Philip Professor of Technology in the Department of Engineering of the [[University of Cambridge]] from 2002 to 2016.

==Education==
Born in [[New Plymouth]], [[New Zealand]], Kelly went to [[Francis Douglas Memorial College]] in his High-school years, graduating he then went on to study at the [[Victoria University of Wellington]] for a BSc and MSc.<ref name=csap-bio/> He came to England in 1971 to study for a PhD at Cambridge under [[Volker Heine]].{{citation needed|date=December 2016}}

==Career==
After finishing his PhD in 1974, he worked for seven years on the electronic structure of metals and semiconductors as a post-doc researcher. Kelly joined the [[GEC Hirst Research Centre]] in 1981, working on the development of microwave devices. From 1992 to 2002 he was Professor of Physics and Electronics at the [[University of Surrey]]. From 2003 to 2005 he was the Executive Director of the [[Cambridge–MIT Institute]].<ref name=csap-bio>{{cite web |url=https://www.csap.cam.ac.uk/network/michael-kelly/ |title=Professor Michael Kelly - Emeritus Professor of Engineering, University of Cambridge |website=Centre for Science and Policy, University of Cambridge |access-date=28 November 2022}}</ref>

He was Prince Philip Professor of Technology working in the Solid State Electronics and Nanoscale Science group in the [[Electrical Engineering]] division of the [[Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge|Department of Engineering]], [[University of Cambridge]] from 2002 to 2016.<ref name=csap-bio/><ref name=eng-20101016>{{cite web |url=http://www3.eng.cam.ac.uk/~mjk1/ |title=Prof M.J. Kelly |website=Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge |date=16 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191225164709/http://www3.eng.cam.ac.uk/~mjk1/ |archive-date=25 December 2019}}</ref> He is an Emeritus Fellow of [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge]].<ref name=trinity-2021>{{cite web |url=https://issuu.com/trinityhallcamb/docs/s0883_trinity_hall_review_os_21_sg_digital |title=Trinity Hall Review 2020/21 |page=40 |website=Trinity Hall, University of Cambridge |via=issuu.com |year=2021 |access-date=28 November 2022}}</ref>

In 2018 Kelly became trustee of the [[Renewable Energy Foundation]] and in 2019 a trustee of the [[Global Warming Policy Foundation]].<ref name=guardian-20220405>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2022/apr/05/charity-linked-to-uk-anti-onshore-wind-campaigns-active-again-renewable-energy-foundation |title=Charity linked to UK anti-onshore wind campaigns active again |last=Horton |first=Helena |newspaper=The Guardian |date=5 April 2022 |access-date=28 November 2022}}</ref><ref name=charity-1107360>{{cite web |url=https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/charity-search/-/charity-details/4011707/trustees |title=The Renewable Energy Foundation |id=Charity no. 1107360 |publisher=Charity Commission |access-date=28 November 2022}}</ref><ref name=charity-1131448>{{cite web |url=https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/charity-search/-/charity-details/4047036/trustees |title=The Global Warming Policy Foundation |id=Charity no. 1131448 |publisher=Charity Commission |access-date=28 November 2022}}</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1993 and won its [[Hughes Medal]] in 2006.  He was formerly the Chief Scientific Adviser to the [[Department for Communities and Local Government]].<ref>House of Commons, Minutes of Evidence, [https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200708/cmselect/cmdius/c1194-i/c119402.htm HC 1194-i] (2008)</ref> He was elected in 1998 as a [[Fellow]] of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]].<ref name=raeng-lof>{{cite web |url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows?fa=k |title=List of Fellows |website=Royal Academy of Engineering |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706181934/https://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows?fa=k |archive-date=6 July 2020}}</ref>

== Climatic Research Unit investigation ==
In 2010, Kelly was named by the [[Royal Society]] and the [[University of East Anglia]] to an independent scientific assessment panel to investigate the [[Climatic Research Unit email controversy]].<ref>[http://www.uea.ac.uk/mac/comm/media/press/CRUstatements/SAPannounce CRU Scientific Assessment Panel announced] 22 Mar 2010</ref> The panel concluded that there was "no evidence of any deliberate scientific malpractice in any of the work of the Climatic Research Unit."<ref name="SAP-Report">
